original_question: Let K be compact. Is the weak Baire measurability of the supremum norm on C(K), viewed as measurability with respect to Ba(C(K), w), equivalent to weak*-separability of the dual unit ball B_{C(K)^*} or of the whole dual space C(K)^*?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.3 in Section 2.1 of arXiv:1607.07787 ("Problems in measurability in Banach spaces"), which is the later restatement of open problem (A) in Section 3.3 of the cited paper [11], A weak* separable C(K)* space whose unit ball is not weak* separable.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of the paper's question very well: it is about a compact space K, the supremum norm on C(K), measurability with respect to the weak Baire sigma-algebra Ba(C(K), w), and whether that measurability is tied to weak*-separability of either the dual unit ball B_{C(K)^*} or the whole dual space C(K)^*.
missing_details: K should be assumed compact Hausdorff; in arXiv:1607.07787 all topological spaces are Hausdorff.
C(K) is the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K, equipped with the supremum norm ||·||_∞.
The measurability in question is the measurability of the map ||·||_∞: C(K) -> R with respect to the weak Baire sigma-algebra Ba(C(K), w).
B_{C(K)^*} means the closed unit ball of C(K)^*, and weak*-separability is with respect to the canonical weak* topology on C(K)^*.

The surrounding context includes the one-way implications B_{C(K)^*} weak*-separable => ||·||_∞ is Ba(C(K), w)-measurable => C(K)^* weak*-separable; the open problem asks whether either converse holds in the specific case of the supremum norm on C(K).

The official wording asks about two possible equivalences: with weak*-separability of B_{C(K)^*}, or with weak*-separability of C(K)^*. It does not state that those two separability properties are themselves equivalent.
If one stays closest to Problem 2.3 in arXiv:1607.07787, one should omit the extra follow-up from the earlier paper asking specifically about the special compact space constructed there.
refined_question: Let K be a compact Hausdorff space, and let C(K) be the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K with the supremum norm ||·||_∞. Is the map ||·||_∞: C(K) -> R measurable with respect to the weak Baire sigma-algebra Ba(C(K), w)? Equivalently, in this C(K)-supremum-norm setting, is Ba(C(K), w)-measurability of ||·||_∞ equivalent to weak*-separability of the closed unit ball B_{C(K)^*}, or at least to weak*-separability of the whole dual space C(K)^*?
justification: The draft is essentially a close paraphrase of the paper's official open problem. In arXiv:1607.07787, Problem 2.3 asks exactly whether measurability of the supremum norm with respect to Ba(C(K), w) is equivalent to weak*-separability of B_{C(K)^*} or of C(K)^*. The nearby discussion records the implication chain B_{C(K)^*} weak*-separable => norm measurable => C(K)^* weak*-separable, explains that the converse implications fail for arbitrary equivalent norms, and says the unresolved case is when C(K) carries its natural supremum norm. The earlier source paper [11] gives the same question as open problem (A) in Section 3.3 after proving partial measurability results on norm-dense subsets (Theorem 3.10) and, under a Kunen-cardinal assumption, on a larger dense family (Theorem 3.22). So the most paper-faithful sharpening of your draft is a self-contained restatement of Problem 2.3 with the implicit assumptions and notation made explicit.
